newsitem.title: UK: Liberty order system to route via Reuters.
newsitem.headline: Liberty order system to route via Reuters.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Monday it signed a deal with a division of the Cedel Group Company to make its Liberty InterTrade Direct order routing system available through Reuters' own information network.

The routing system will be available on Reuters' systems in mid-1997 through an integrated interface, said a statement from the UK electronic information giant. Reuters customers will be able to have direct access to the Liberty routing system via Reuters Terminals for their equities orders.

A Reuter statement said: "The InterTrade Direct system will enable order routing to any of the current executing brokers on Liberty, either on a cross border or domestic basis, and can also be used to route orders internally within an organisation."
Liberty claims the transaction -- from entering the order to its execution and confirmation -- takes place within seconds.

Jeff Metter, Liberty general manager said "Reuters global capacity strengthens our position in the market by complementing other vendor agreements already in place and gives us access to many markets of liquidity both domestically and cross border."

Kim Waters, Reuters international marketing director of messaging and contributions products, said of the benefit to its customers "They will have the option of access to Liberty's trading capability from our screens. A trader should be able to access price information, news and analysis and can route orders as well as receive confirmation of a trade with an audit trail."
